# THE HERMETIC PRINCIPLES

*The seven axioms of the Kybalion weighed against the deck: four land with
uncanny precision, one was already this system's founding sentence, and one
collides with the Caster's Law so directly that the collision is the most
valuable thing on the page. Held as source, never endorsement.*

## I · THE SOURCE, DATED HONESTLY

Two strata wear the name Hermetic, and this room takes its sources with
their true dates. The old stratum is the Corpus Hermeticum and the Emerald
Tablet, late antique texts whose most famous sentence, as above, so below,
is genuinely ancient. The younger stratum is the Kybalion of 1908, a New
Thought work published by Three Initiates, in all likelihood William Walker
Atkinson, which dressed its seven principles in Hermes' name and an implied
antiquity they do not have. The seven principles weighed below are the
Kybalion's list. Naming that is not a dismissal; a book may be recent and
still be right. It is the same discipline this shelf applied to the Tesla
folklore: a source enters with its provenance showing, or it does not
enter.

## II · WHERE THE DECK AGREES

**Vibration.** Nothing rests; everything moves; everything vibrates. This
was never a principle the deck needed to import, because it is the deck's
founding sentence: the first card is the unstruck string, every card is an
interval, and form is the shape a sound leaves. The full weighing of that
claim lives in the chart of the language of the birds and is not repeated
here.

**Polarity.** The Kybalion holds that opposites are identical in nature and
differ only in degree. The deck's involution says this with arithmetic:
every card and its counter share the same interval and the same winding,
differing only in hand, so that a dyad is one sound heard against its own
mirror, and the pair beats rather than argues. Of the seven, this is the
principle the deck states most exactly, and it was derived from the knot
map, not adopted.

**Correspondence.** As above, so below. The deck is built of one triad
repeated at every scale: three states, three layers, three suits, three
positions, and each suit is one full turn of the same nine-wheel. The sky
instruments read the heavens into the identical grammar the smallest
reading uses. But this room holds the ancient sentence with a modern
discipline: correspondence is a licence only at the resolution the survey
supports. The chart of the watches draws that boundary, and it is what
separates a map of time's qualities from the unsurveyed precision this
principle has historically been used to excuse.

**Rhythm.** Everything flows, out and in; all things rise and fall. The
deck's settling relations, computed rather than composed, drain every road
to stillness or to pure tone and then home again; the moon waxes and wanes
through every witnessed cast; the crank turns the year. The pendulum is
real here, though the deck states it as arithmetic rather than as maxim.

## III · WHERE THE DECK REFUSES

**Cause and effect.** The Kybalion's sixth principle abolishes chance:
chance, it says, is but a name for law not recognised. The Caster's Law is
built on the opposite conviction, and the difference is not negotiable.
This instrument treats chance as the honest ground of a cast: entropy
gathered and declared, seeds published so any hand can replay the deal, and
the expectation of chance spoken in the same breath as every count, one
card at home, chance expects one. Chance here is not ignorance of hidden
law. It is the one guest that cannot be bribed, which is why the readings
can be trusted at all. A doctrine in which nothing is truly random would
dissolve the Aleatory Law and, with it, the instrument's honesty. On this
principle the deck does not merely differ from the Kybalion; it is built
against it.

**Gender.** The Kybalion runs on twos: masculine and feminine principles in
everything, polarity doubled into a metaphysic. The deck is ternary by
construction, still, flowing and turning, and its pairs are mirror-handed
rather than gendered. Where the twofold systems and the threefold part
company, and what each buys, is the standing subject of the chart of the
two and the three; the deck's answer to duality everywhere is simply its
own arithmetic.

**Mentalism.** The All is Mind, says the first principle. The deck neither
affirms nor denies it; the claim stands outside what an honest instrument
can weigh, and so it is held the way this shelf holds vibration as physics:
with respect, at arm's length, and with no reading resting on it.

## IV · WHAT THIS CHART REFUSES

No principle enters a reading. No card means polarity, no spread
illustrates rhythm, and no correspondence licenses a precision the survey
cannot support. The seven are held beside the deck as a source among
sources: where they agree, the agreement was derived independently and the
derivation is the evidence; where they part, the parting is recorded as
carrying exactly the weight of the agreement.

## PROVENANCE

*Entered 23 July 2026 at the architect's question, on a day given to the
structure of the deck, following the language of the birds onto the
references shelf. The Kybalion's date and likely authorship are the common
scholarly record; the Corpus Hermeticum's antiquity likewise. The
correspondences cited are derived in the sealed canon and its computed
charts, none of them arranged for this comparison. Nothing here predicts,
and nothing here prescribes.*
